comment: Cross-surface reference-image capability expectations. `capabilities.reference_images` on the generation profile is the SINGLE authority for whether a checkpoint takes ordered reference images, how many, whether the first one is the edit target, and how references relate to `source_image`. `mold_core::generation_profile::reference_images_for_recipe` answers it once; the Rust test in mold-core and the vitest `studio/lib/flux2ReferenceParity.test.ts` both read this file, so a drift on either side fails CI. Absence of the block on the wire means an OLDER SERVER, never a refusal — clients fall back to their pre-profile family sniff (`legacyReferenceImages`), which knows FLUX.2 [dev] and Qwen-Image-Edit and deliberately does NOT know FLUX.2 [klein]: a host that predates this contract has no Klein reference engine.

relations.replaces: The references ARE the conditioning: `source_image`, `mask_image` and ControlNet inputs are refused alongside them (qwen-image-edit, flux2-dev).
relations.exclusive: The checkpoint renders from a source image OR from references, never both in one pass. Both wells are offered; whichever holds media parks the other (flux2 klein).
relations.combines: References and a source image travel together. No shipped recipe uses this today.

models.comment: FLUX.2 [dev] multi-reference editing, the pre-contract behaviour every client used to sniff by name.
The distilled Klein tier takes the identical reference protocol upstream and keeps img2img, the repaint mask, and LoRA — hence `exclusive` rather than `replaces`.
The undistilled 9B base tier samples with a real unconditional branch; its reference contract is the same.
The first image is the edit TARGET, which is why the shared Target well renders above the strip. No server-side count bound.
FLUX.1 takes no reference images (Kontext is a separate checkpoint, filed as its own PR). Hidden with `max_count: 0` — the block is present and says no.
